samples.summary: Vertical-move caller of findVisualLine() still uses the legacy hard-coded 'forward' boundary default, disagreeing with the affinity-aware helpers this PR introduced
samples.evidence: packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:4165 calls `findVisualLine(lb, pos)` with no third argument, so a wrap-boundary offset resolves with the helper's legacy default `'forward'` (packages/docs/src/view/visual-line.ts:24) even when `this.cursor.lineAffinity === 'backward'` — the cursor's own default (packages/docs/src/view/cursor.ts:13) and exactly the state the new tests reach after `End`. Every other consumer of the changed contract now defaults to `this.cursor.lineAffinity` (text-editor.ts:4001, 4053, 4061). Consequence: with the caret at a character-wrap boundary with backward affinity, this branch treats it as being on line i+1, so the ArrowUp 'first visual line → jump to line start' and ArrowDown 'last visual line → jump to line end' shortcuts use the wrong line's lineStart/lineEnd. Fix belongs on the new code: pass `this.cursor.lineAffinity` here. This line predates the reviewed delta; raised because it is the one unupdated consumer of the contract the PR changed.

samples.summary: Two affinity-taking helpers ship opposite defaults ('forward' vs 'backward'), so argument-less calls resolve wrap boundaries inconsistently
samples.evidence: packages/docs/src/view/visual-line.ts:24 defaults `lineAffinity` to `'forward'`, while packages/docs/src/view/pagination.ts:385 and packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:5099 default the same-named parameter to `'backward'`. Callers that omit the argument therefore get different boundary resolution depending on which helper they reach — e.g. `getPixelForPosition` (backward) versus `findVisualLine` at text-editor.ts:4165 (forward) for the same caret. Aligning on the cursor's `'backward'` would remove the trap for future callers.

finding.summary: moveVertical() still calls findVisualLine() without affinity, so it resolves a wrap boundary to the *later* line while the rest of the editor now resolves it to the caret's line
finding.evidence: packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:4165 `const info = findVisualLine(lb, pos);` — the only other caller of the changed helper, left on the new `'forward'` default. Meanwhile getPixelForPosition() two lines earlier (4104) already hit-tests with `this.cursor.lineAffinity`, so the two halves of moveVertical disagree at a boundary. This inconsistency is newly reachable from the keyboard: after this change `handleEnd` (2799 + `cursor.moveTo(newPos)` at 2806, which defaults affinity to 'backward' per cursor.ts:28) reliably parks the caret exactly on a character-wrap boundary with 'backward' affinity — the very state the new test at packages/docs/test/view/visual-line-affinity.test.ts:151 creates. In that state findVisualLine returns lineIndex i+1, so the `isFirstLine` special case at 4168/4170 (jump to line start on ArrowUp from the first visual line) and the symmetric `isLastLine` case at 4174 no longer fire, and ArrowUp/ArrowDown at the boundary can appear to do nothing. The project's own todo (docs/tasks/active/20260822-docs-visual-line-affinity-todo.md:59) declares this a non-goal, which is why I flag it at medium confidence — but the non-goal reasoning ('its findVisualLine use is only a first/last-line check') is exactly the check that breaks. Fix belongs at text-editor.ts:4165 (pass `this.cursor.lineAffinity`).

verdict.reason: Verified in-repo: findVisualLine() gained a lineAffinity parameter defaulting to 'forward' (visual-line.ts:21-25, boundary rule :38-39), and getVisualLineRange/Start/End were threaded with this.cursor.lineAffinity (text-editor.ts:3999-4063). The remaining consumer at text-editor.ts:4165 calls findVisualLine(lb, pos) with no affinity, so it resolves a wrap-boundary offset to line i+1 while the same function's pixel hit-test at text-editor.ts:4104 uses this.cursor.lineAffinity — the isFirstLine/isLastLine special cases at 4168-4177 are therefore computed on a different visual line than the caret is drawn on. The state is keyboard-reachable: handleEnd (2797-2806) calls cursor.moveTo(newPos) which defaults affinity to 'backward' (cursor.ts:28), and getVisualLineEnd only trims trailing spaces (4067-4073), so on character-wrapped text End lands exactly on the boundary (the scenario in test/view/visual-line-affinity.test.ts:141-157); ArrowUp/ArrowDown then enters moveVertical (2746-2747) preserving that affinity (2776). The page-boundary branch (4118-4158) falls through when no adjacent page exists, so control does reach 4162-4179 in a single-block document, where layout.blocks[0] === pos.blockId holds. No guard makes it unreachable, the code is exactly as quoted, and it is squarely in the blast-radius lane (changed helper contract, unupdated consumer outside the diff). The repo todo's 'non-goal' note is data, and its rationale is the very check that flips.
